values.note: Check in at the park office on arrival; pay in advance at the office (Saturday and Sunday 9 am to noon), by drop box at the office or shop, by mail, or by card over the phone. No online booking.

note: Clay County park on Milford Lake at the east edge of Wakefield, on Corps land: gravel pull-in loops with many seasonal campers, a mowed lawn between the east loop road and the shore, and a boat ramp at the north end. --Claude
summary: County page + 2024 rate sheet + 2025 rules: $25-35 (30 A / 50 A / sewer) confirmed; hookups now 50 A + water + sewer (was 30 A); showers/dump confirmed; check-in/pay at office (booking note). Season Apr 15-Oct 15 not stated by any county page (left). Waterfront lead lakefront -> lakeview (pads ~120 m back behind a loop road). Seasonal-heavy (Corps lease lets 75% go seasonal).
flags: WATERFRONT lead (apply.py doesn't write it): stored LAKEFRONT is not earned. On imagery (180 m frame centred 39.2115,-97.0060) the easternmost pads sit 110-130 m from the shore, behind the campground's own perimeter loop road and a mowed lawn ~100 m wide; nothing is on the water. Propose LAKEVIEW (open lawn, lake visible from the east row).

LONG-STAY character (a human call): the county page bills it 'Stay the weekend or spend a season'; the rate sheet is mostly monthly/seasonal plans; the rules carry three pages of seasonal-camper regulations; and the Corps' KC District criteria linked from the page let up to 75% of the sites be seasonal, with at least 25% kept for first-come transient campers. It sells nights ($25 30 A posted), Google 4.4/76, so I'd keep it, but it is on the seasonal end of the spectrum.

SEASON: stored Apr 15-Oct 15 (derived from note prose) is stated by none of the county pages. They say seasonal campers pay April-September, units must be gone Dec 1-end of February, and the Corps lets seasonal sites be occupied Mar 1-Nov 30. Left as stored; it remains unconfirmed.
